506a4ac76f9f46e9d49814cd6611a23c73600507: Wildschönau offers 98 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for a stay of 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 45 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the flow of skiers in high season. Wildschönau has kept an authentic mountain-village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. The altitude of Wildschönau (870 m at the bottom, 2030 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Wildschönau is clearly high: €72 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Wildschönau keeps its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.

50ea4b44e24bf575276fbfa23ed3a2a02909098a: Wendelstein is a low-key resort on a modest scale, with 11 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts whatsoever. Technical terrain is king at Wendelstein: with 37 black and 63 red runs on the programme, confident skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are practised here, often in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. Wendelstein's modest altitude, starting at 791 m and topping out at 1723 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly recommended. At 49€ the day pass places Wendelstein among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Wendelstein doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
